production_rules: Create four finished, visually and persuasively distinct English thumbnails per request. By default, deliver one Canva design with four editable pages unless the user requests another format. Use native Canva commands driven by design JSON, without PPTX or full-thumbnail image flattening. Code-rendered local previews are allowed.

Structure 01: Before left, After right. Structure 04: Before lower-left inset, After large right photo. Put Before/After labels inside their respective photos at bottom-right. User confirmation of AI concept roles is not proof of actual product-use results.
Use 3-4 verified benefit bullets or short sentences in information-heavy benefit sections, not a single tagline.

Photo-first layouts keep the After portrait dominant while explaining the product: place product name and a short benefit above the left Before inset, then compact verified explanatory copy below it. Concise copy must still be informative.

Use clear benefit/concern-led beauty copy; editorial tone must not obscure the meaning. Read click-through-copy.md for concrete functional support and destination-specific CTAs. Do not make unsupported numerical, ingredient, or efficacy claims.

Freshly write all four main headlines for each new request, including 03-question-led. Keep layouts reusable but wording flexible, based on the current appeal, verified product facts, and persuasion angle. Vary sentence structure as well as wording; do not habitually reuse the concern-list plus What next? formula. Preserve prior copy only when explicitly requested or outside the scope of a targeted revision.

Use the latest user-supplied assets/beplain-logo.png at top-left on every thumbnail; preserve proportions, artwork and alpha during placement and upload. Do not add a white box/badge. Choose a light composition behind the black logo rather than moving it right.

When retaining supplied originals for revisions, preserve all text, geometry, fonts, colors, crops, and layer order exactly. Default to interleaved original/revised page pairs unless the user explicitly requests another order.

In question-led copy, move from the concern to a concrete verified benefit or ingredient and a clear next action; avoid generic concern repetition. Keep wording fresh unless the user has explicitly approved it.

Establish enough distinct verified explanation before adjusting type scale and spacing. Larger type supports hierarchy but does not replace missing information. Judge headline, support, line height and gaps together; avoid both accidental voids and cramped body text.
Default canvas is 1600x1600px. New sets have four pages in one Canva file; revision page counts follow actual requested originals and copies, not a historical eight-page job.
Separate canonical design intent from runtime IDs, uploads, command responses and verification evidence. Block missing assets or ambiguous mappings; retain failed attempts.

Inspect actual Canva previews and individual editability. Preview locally, apply JSON to native objects, show finished Canva previews before any tool-required save approval, commit after approval and verify saved metadata.

Name the actual Canva file MM.DD for the Friday of the user request's Monday–Sunday week. Use explicit local request date and timezone, keep that date for the job, and verify the saved title. Example: 2026-10-10 → 10.09.

For copy/CTR-wording revisions, preserve the supplied theme, type families/sizes, layout and portrait framing. Use exact native text substitutions; shorten and rephrase before any visual change. Explicit user redesign instructions override this scope default.

First-pass copy must connect relevance, verified benefits, concrete support and the real next step. Ingredient names and vague support slogans alone are insufficient. Keep quick points and explanatory prose distinct; do not cut useful functions merely to make the layout sparse.
Inspect natural portrait framing and native text reflow before showing the set. Do not create awkward cutout-like crops or enlarge type to compensate for insufficient copy.
Describe copy revisions as intended to improve click motivation, not as a measured CTR increase. Keep current product claims and sources in the job evidence.
One invocation includes internal comparison/correction of all actual Canva pages to the matching quality reference before presenting the set. Tool-required final save approval is still observed.

For new sets, read appeal-led-production.md: four concise distinct overview benefits followed by specific problem/solution, focused visual comparison and complementary support. Default remains four pages chosen from five structures; an explicitly requested one-structure demo is one page.

Use supplied/authorized photos with crop/scale in Canva. When appeal-specific AI photo preparation is also requested, complete it upstream with ImageGen, retain provenance and visibly disclose concepts. Do not edit skin using code or present concepts as proof.
Structure 05 uses the same anatomical region, pose and crop scale before/after, within source views 0–45 degrees. This intentional close-up is allowed; accidental cropping to fit text is not.

Latest type preference: enlarge useful body/benefit phrases, use bold and restrained brand-color emphasis, shorten wordy copy instead of shrinking type. Historical font sizes/paragraph lengths are no longer mandatory for new sets.
Use a packshot only from supplied or user-authorized official assets. Competitor reference photography, packaging and results are not beplain evidence.
reference_review_protocol: Explicit user comparisons of supplied visible images are already-confirmed style feedback; record them directly without another yes/no round. The research protocol below applies when discovering new references.
Research official, directly visible beauty-brand images in small batches.
Ask the user yes/no about the whole visual and record any element-level reason they volunteer.
Do not treat an image that failed to display as an approval or rejection.
Never copy another brand's photo, logo, exact slogan, or unsupported claims into the deliverable.
